title: What a Java constructor is
answer: A constructor is a special class member used to initialize a newly created object. It has the same name as the class and no return type, and it runs as part of a normal `new` object-creation expression after superclass initialization. Constructors can validate input and establish invariants before the caller receives the reference. In AeroTopo, the `Orthomosaic` constructor delegates common state to `Product`, validates GSD, and stores the instance value.
